title: Nudging a stalled reader
statement: How to nudge a reader who stalls or keeps guessing; nothing in my engine does yet.
detail:
The lesson engine's playtest refuses idle actions because nothing in the runtime nudges a reader who is stuck, and a
guesser in a choice block has no attempt ceiling (`g9/transformer/src/quality/playtest.js`); a director that adapts is
planned for a later stage (`g9/transformer/v05/README.md`). To settle it: the scripted stuck reader and guesser finish
with a nudge, and a person-labelled set shows the nudge comes at the right moment.

evidence.quote: the "not so fast" nudge is non-blocking and can be skipped by clicking Next twice.
The system needs three outcomes, not two: promote, keep practising, or switch to corrective instruction.
A mastery system that lacks an explicit “switch mode” state will inevitably turn persistence into the hidden criterion for passing.
when a learner is failing, we currently just let them keep attempting items.
iter-3 `silent`/"I don't know" branch authored + gated in 18/18 but **can never fire** (any tap resolves elsewhere; no timeout / "I'm not sure" affordance)
scaffold-down (feedback / reframe / supply / model / engage) is actually reachable for the child who freezes or says "I don't know"

evidence.path: SUPERSEDED — see v2.1_ WITW Lesson 1 learning walkthrough v2 (table format).md
evidence.quote: Open answers route to full / brief / partial / off-track / silent paths | Every path teaches; the silent child is taught first, then re-asked easier
When a child struggles, scaffold down by giving feedback, reframing, supplying an answer, offering a model to mimic, or simply keeping the child engaged (Zucker et al., 2020).
Now a quiet "I'm not sure yet" door routes there.
